summary: 掌声既表达赞赏，也曾让古罗马统治者判断民意，或被有组织的喝彩者操纵。文章沿古代剧场、职业鼓掌团和现代演出礼仪写到网络点赞，展示观众反馈的形式和持续时间如何改变。
logic: 组织喝彩与职业鼓掌团

paragraphs.brief: 鼓掌作为剧场行为的早期出现。
sentences: Scholars aren’t quite sure about the origins of applause, but the form that is still most common, clapping the hands together, was formalized in Western culture during and after performances.
学者们不太确定掌声的起源，但最常见的形式，一起拍手，在表演期间和之后，在西方文化中正式化。
During the time of the Roman Republic (509 BC – 27 BC) the common way to end a play was for the chief actor to yell ‘Valete et plaudite!’
在罗马共和国时期(公元前509年-公元前27年)，结束一场戏的共同方式是首席演员大喊“Valete et plaudite!”
(‘Goodbye and applause!’) thus signaling to the audience that it was time for them to give praise by striking hands and making explosive noise.
(再见和掌声! ) 从而向观众发出信号，他们现在应该用拳头和爆炸性噪音来赞美。
It’s no surprise, then, that this became a means of crowd manipulation.
这并不奇怪，所以，这成了一个操纵人群的手段。
Rome saw the rise of a professional class of applauders, or ‘people who clapped for their dinner’, hired to infiltrate crowds and manipulate their reaction to performances.
罗马看到一群专业的鼓掌者，或“为他们的晚餐鼓掌的人”，被雇来渗透人群，操纵他们对表演的反应。
Actors would hire a dozen or so people to spread out among their audiences and prolong the applause, or, if they were feeling especially bold, to start ‘spontaneous’ chants and shouts of praise.
演员们会雇用十几个人，在观众中传播，延长掌声，或者，如果他们感到特别大胆，开始“自大”的歌喊和赞美。

paragraphs.brief: 政治人物用掌声衡量自己的声望。
sentences: The Roman Republic came to an end and was replaced by the Roman Empire (27 BC – 476 AD) where applause became a way for leaders to interact directly with their citizens.
罗马共和国结束了，代之以罗马帝国(公元前27年-公元前476年)，在那里，掌声成为领导人与公民直接互动的一种方式。
One of the chief methods they used to estimate their standing with the people was gauging the greetings they got when they entered the arena.
他们用来评估自己在人民中的地位的主要方法之一是衡量他们进入竞技场时得到的问候。
Leaders became astute at reading the volume, the rhythm, and the length of the crowd’s claps for clues about how well they were doing as officials and lawmakers.
领袖们在阅读群众拍手的音量，节奏和长度时变得很聪明，寻找他们作为官员和立法者表现的线索。
‘We should think of it as an ancient type of opinion poll,’ says Greg Aldrete, a professor of history.
格雷格·阿德雷特历史教授：“我们应该把它视为古老的民意测验。”
‘This is how you gauge the people.’
你这样判断众人。
Roman leaders were gathering data about people by listening to applause.
罗马领导人正在通过聆听掌声来收集人们的数据。

paragraphs.brief: 根据掌声判断对手是否受欢迎。
sentences: Clever leaders of the ancient world researched their rivals, too.
古代世界的聪明领袖也研究过对手

Cicero, the Roman lawyer, would send friends to stand around outside the arena, taking notes to see what kind of greeting each official got when he entered, the better to see who was beloved by the people, and who was not.
罗马律师西塞罗会派朋友站在竞技场外注意看每个官员进场时都得到了什么样的问候越看谁被人民所爱谁是没有
They had a lot of information to assess.
他们有很多信息要评估
‘Ancient crowds were more interactive than they are today,’ Aldrete points out.
Aldrete指出：「古老的人群比今天更具有互动性。
‘There was a lot of back and forth between speakers and crowds.
喇叭声和人群之间有很多前后的交汇
And particularly in the Greco-Roman world, crowds, especially in cities, were really good at communicating messages through rhythmic clapping, sometimes coupled with shouts.’
特别是在希腊-罗马世界，人群，特别是城市人群，非常擅长通过节奏的鼓掌，有时还伴之以喊叫来传递信息。
The coding was, he says, invaluable when assessing an orator’s fortunes.
他说，在评估导师的财富时，编码非常宝贵。

paragraphs.brief: 古人除拍手之外的喝彩方式。
sentences: Around the first century AD, those systems of applause became more and more elaborate.
大约在公元前一世纪，这些掌声系统变得越来越复杂。
Applause no longer meant, simply, ‘claps’.
掌声已不再是简单的“拍手”的意思。
While Greco-Roman audiences certainly smacked their palms together the same way we do today, their overall strategies of applause were much more varied than clapping alone.
虽然希腊罗马观众的掌掌声肯定和我们今天一样，但是他们的掌声总体策略比单独鼓掌要多得多。
Crowds expressed degrees of approval of the person or persons before them, ranging from claps, to snaps (of the finger and thumb), to waves (of the edge of the toga).
人群对前面的人表示一定程度的认可，从拍手到(手指和拇指)断裂，到(陀伽边缘)波浪不等。

The emperor Aurelian decided to replace this gesture by waving a special handkerchief instead, a prop which he then distributed to all Roman citizens, so they would never be without a way to praise him.
奥雷利安皇帝决定用手帕代替这个姿态，他挥动了特殊的手帕，这是他随后分发给所有罗马公民的道具，因此他们永远不会没有办法赞扬他。

paragraphs.brief: 假意喝彩的复兴和衰落。
sentences: Although style of applause may have changed over the centuries, the need to manipulate remained.
虽然几个世纪以来掌声的风格可能已经改变，但操纵的必要性仍然存在。
16th-century French poet Jean Daurat is credited with bringing back the Roman practice of hiring professional applauders.
16世纪的法国诗人让·达拉特将罗马雇用职业嘉宾的做法带回了这里
In France, this group became known as a ‘claque’.
在法国，这个团体被称为“claque”。
Daurat handed out tickets to his own performances to people who promised to applaud at the end.
Daurat向那些最后承诺要鼓掌的人发放了自己的演出票。
By the early 1820s, claques had become institutionalized, with an agency in Paris specializing in the distribution of the claqueurs’ services.
到20世纪20年代初，锁会已经制度化，在巴黎有一个专门提供锁会服务的机构。

The historian William B. Cohen describes the intricate price lists agencies of this kind would hand out to potential patrons: polite clapping would cost this many francs, enthusiastic applause would cost this many.
历史学家威廉·科恩描述了这种复杂的价格清单，它们会交给潜在的赞助人：礼貌的鼓掌会花费这么多法郎，热情的掌声会花费这么多。

The claque also underwent a kind of classification: the rieurs (laughers) would laugh loudly at the jokes; the pleureurs (criers) would feign tears in reaction to performances; the commissaires (officers) would learn a play or a piece of music by heart and then call attention to its best parts.
Clque也经历了一种分类：那些骑马的人会大笑笑话；那些骑马的在表演中装出眼泪；那些警察会从心底里学一首剧或一首音乐，然后引起人们对其最佳部分的注意。
This practice spread to Milan, to Vienna, and to London before falling out of fashion.
这种做法蔓延到米兰，维也纳，伦敦之后就过时了
The claque lost its power once people became aware of its tricks.
一旦人们意识到它的诡计 Clque就失去了它的力量

paragraphs.brief: 音乐演出如何改变鼓掌礼仪。
sentences: And clapping itself evolved.
鼓掌本身进化。
In the 18th century, symphonies and concerts became more serious, aligning themselves with the reverence and spirituality associated with religious ceremonies.
在18世纪，交响乐和音乐会变得更加严肃，与宗教仪式相关的崇敬和精神精神一致。
Knowing when to maintain silence, as well as when to clap, became a mark of sophistication, a kind of code for audiences to learn.
知道何时保持缄默何时拍手成为了精密的标志一种供观众学习的代码
Applause became a matter of ‘do’ or ‘don’t’, so losing many old shades of meaning.
掌声变成“做”或“不”的问题，所以失去了许多旧的表达面。
Those changes changed performers, too.
这些变化也改变了表演者。
Applause became much less of a true dialogue with an audience, especially so with opera, where the singers saw it as part of a basic transaction with the crowd.
掌声比和观众进行真正的对话要少得多，特别是歌剧，歌星们把歌剧视为与观众的基本交易的一部分。
So by the time the 19th century arrived, applause had become standardized and institutionalized, and had become an expectation rather than the reward it used to be.
到了19世纪，掌声已经标准化和制度化，并且变成了一种期望，而不是它曾经的回报。

paragraphs.brief: 传播范围空前广泛的新式掌声。
sentences: In the 21st century we’re reinventing applause, to make it what it used to be: a coded form of communication.
21世纪，我们重新掌声，把它变成过去的东西：一种编码化的通讯方式。
More and more the digital world allows us to link and like and share through our devices.
数字世界越来越使我们能够通过我们的设备连接、喜欢和分享。
By connecting with others in this way, we become part of the performance by participating in it, demonstrating our appreciation by amplifying and extending the show through commenting and praising.
通过以这种方式与他人建立联系，我们通过参与这一活动，通过评论和赞扬来扩大和扩展这一节目，表明我们的赞赏，从而成为其业绩的一部分。
Our kind of applause matters more now, in many ways, because it is no longer momentary and short-lived, but is far more permanent instead.
我们的那种掌声现在在许多方面更重要，因为它不再是短暂和短暂的，而是更加持久。

flow: 从剧场欢呼到政治风向
古罗马剧本早已提示观众鼓掌，政治人物随后既听自己的掌声，也观察竞争者得到怎样的回应。
看喝彩怎样被组织和操纵

从音乐厅的时机到网络的范围
音乐演出形成了何时应安静、何时可鼓掌的规矩，而网上的赞同甚至可以来自不在现场的人。

items.en: Which TWO of the following statements are true of the ‘claque’ in France?

correct: As a practice in France, it first appeared in the 16th century.
作为一种法国的做法，它最早出现在16世纪。
Claqueurs were divided into different categories.

items.en: In the 18th century, people could show their superiority by understanding when either ________ or applause was appropriate.

items.en: In the 19th century, applause was no longer offered as a ________ to performers.

items.why: 回到对应内容“到了19世纪，掌声已经标准化和制度化，并且变成了一种期望，而不是它曾经的回报”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Nowadays our expressions of approval are seen as ________ in comparison to the applause of the past.

items.why: 题干“Nowadays our expressions of approval”指 G 段的数字时代点赞、分享、评论等。与过去短暂的现场掌声相比，现代“掌声" 更加 permanent,因为会在网络上留下痕迹并持续传播。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 罗马领袖听掌声的强弱和节奏，把它当成了解自身支持度的民意调查。
回到对应内容“到了19世纪，掌声已经标准化和制度化，并且变成了一种期望，而不是它曾经的回报”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: (‘Goodbye and applause!’) thus signaling to the audience ….
“that it was time for them to give praise by striking hands and making explosive noise”补足 signaling 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 signaling 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Actors would hire a dozen or so people to spread out among their audiences and prolong the applause, or, ….
连接词 if 引出“if they were feeling especially bold, to start ‘spontaneous’ chants and shouts of praise”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Whether you clap, cheer or whistle a great public performance, you are following a long tradition.
无论是拍手、欢呼或吹口哨伟大的公共表演，你遵循了一个很长的传统。
